Pixel users report broken always-on display in Android Auto after November update

Even the newest Pixel phones aren't spared.

•

•

•

Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Pixel users report that the November update breaks the always-on display when connected to Android Auto.

• The issue affects multiple generations, including the Pixel 9, Pixel 10, and Pixel 11 series.

• We’ve reached out to Google to see whether it’s aware of the bug and working on a fix.

Google’s November update for Pixel phones has already caused a fair share of headaches, from broken lock screen shortcuts to issues with the always-on display and notifications. It turns out the update may have introduced yet another display-related bug, this time affecting Pixel owners who use Android Auto.

Pixel owners across Reddit and the Android Auto Help community report that their phones’ always-on displays stop working when connected to Android Auto. Instead of showing the time, notifications, and other glanceable information, the screen remains completely black until they disconnect from their cars.

The issue isn’t limited to older Pixels either. While the initial complaint came from a Pixel 9 Pro owner using wireless Android Auto, the Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL are also affected.

Rita El Khoury / Android Authority

Some peculiar things are happening behind the scenes. One Pixel 11 Pro owner noticed that their phone’s display settings blamed Bedtime Mode for disabling AOD, even though neither Bedtime Mode nor Driving Mode was active.

Disabling Driving Mode hasn’t helped, and neither have recent Google Play system updates. A Pixel 11 Pro XL owner briefly regained normal AOD functionality, but the problem returned the following morning. Tapping the screen still wakes the phone, but that defeats the convenience of having an always-on display.

Similar complaints have surfaced outside Google’s English-speaking communities, with a Pixel 9 Pro owner on Taiwanese forum Mobile01 also experiencing broken AOD and having trouble getting Android Auto to launch automatically following the November update.

The good news is that an Android Auto community specialist has already requested diagnostic information from an affected user to help with the investigation. The specialist subsequently confirmed that the team had contacted the user via email for further assistance.

We’ve asked Google if it’s aware of the bug, and we’ll update this article when we hear back.

Unihertz shows off Titan 2 Elite in new white color, and you can pre-order now

You’ll just have to wait a couple months to get it.

•

•

•

Unihertz

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Last week, Unihertz posted a teaser for an upcoming new Titan 2 Elite color option.

• Today the company reveals the Titan 2 Elite in white.

• Unihertz is accepting pre-orders now, but the white model won’t ship for another couple months.

Hardware keyboards are one of those holdovers from the early days of smartphones that just keep popping back up, and if you’re tempted to go a little retro for your next purchase, you’ve now got a new option available to you, as Unihertz reveals its latest color for the Titan 2 Elite.

Last week, we saw Unihertz start teasing a new color option for the Titan 2 Elite. The teaser itself didn’t seem to contain much in the way of hints, leaving us to just speculate as we waited for the announcement. At the very least, we wouldn’t have long to wait, with the manufacturer implying we’d get our answer sometime this month. December still doesn’t arrive for a few more days, but this mystery is already wrapping up, with Unihertz sharing a new white colorway for the Titan 2 Elite, joining the previously available black and orange.

Unihertz

As you can see above, this keyboard is for more than just typing, and like BlackBerry models of yesteryear, you can use the touch-sensitive surface for scrolling through your favorite apps, or even pull up a cursor for finer control.

If all those keys aren’t enough to satisfy your crave for input buttons, Unihertz even gives the Titan 2 Elite a programmable side button that you can set up as a shortcut to whatever you want.

At just about $490, the white Titan 2 Elite costs the same as the orange and black models, but there is another consideration that might impact your purchasing decision — while the other ones ship straight away, the new white edition is currently just in pre-order, and won’t ship for another two months, well into the new year.

That said, Unihertz is prioritizing shipments based on the order in which they’re received, so the longer you hem and haw about it, the further out your ship date is likely to slide.

Was this the new color you were hoping for? Will you be picking up a white Titan 2 Elite, or are you maybe still holding out hope we could get a fourth color option somewhere further down the line? Let us know down in the comments.

items.body: Apple's annual four-day Black Friday through Cyber Monday shopping event is now live in Australia , New Zealand , and Thailand , and it will continue to roll out across Europe, the U.S., and Canada as the calendar turns to Friday, November 27 around the world. In the U.S., Apple's terms and conditions say the promotion begins on November 27 at 12 a.m. Pacific Time and ends on November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. During the shopping event, customers can get an Apple gift card with the purchase of an eligible product at an Apple Store, in the Apple Store app, and on Apple.com. However, the gift card can only be used towards future purchases, and higher immediate discounts on Apple products are frequently available at Amazon and other resellers. In the U.S., Apple is offering gift cards worth up to $300 with the purchase of an eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, Beats Pill speaker, Apple Pencil Pro, and select Magic Keyboards for iPads. For the first time ever, Apple is also offering a $25 gift card with select third-party accessories from brands including Anker, Belkin, Mophie, Nimble, Rains, and Twelve South. The selection includes chargers and MacBook covers. As usual, many of Apple's newer products are excluded from the offer, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, MacBook Neo, latest models of the iPad mini, Apple TV 4K, iMac, and Mac Studio, and more. Refurbished products are also ineligible, and the offer cannot be combined with educational pricing. General technology

Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals an unreleased "SPAC" framework to process anonymized cloud-based Galaxy AI requests.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 10:06 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to “SPAC,” a new Samsung framework for processing AI requests on its servers while keeping them private.

• SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6.

• SPAC doesn’t seem to be active on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung hasn’t announced it either.

Galaxy AI has always made you choose between privacy and capability. Features that run on your phone keep your data there. However, the more capable ones, like Writing assist, Note assist, and generative photo edits, send your data to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s current promise for those is a policy one: Photo Editor, for instance, tells you your image “will be sent to servers for processing… but not stored by Samsung.” If you’d rather not take that on trust and face value, the only option is the “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings, which switches those cloud-based features off entirely.

Apple pitched a way around that trade-off two years ago when it launched Private Cloud Compute with Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. Private Cloud Compute (PCC) promises to extend device-level privacy to server-side AI processing: your request still goes to a server, but it’s encrypted, anonymized, and processed in a way that even Apple says it can’t access. Google and Meta have since built their own versions, with Google promising your personal data stays private to you and is not accessible to anyone else, “not even Google.” Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests Samsung is building its own take on the idea, and it looks a lot like Apple’s.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Samsung’s “SPAC” and “Arcane” are new in One UI 9.5

Digging through One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra over the past week, we found a new Samsung SDK called “SPAC” inside four apps: Photo Editor, IntelliVoiceService (Samsung’s speech and language service), Smart Capture, and PhotoRemasterService. None of these apps had it in One UI 9.

Based on the code, SPAC seemingly connects to a server-side gateway that Samsung’s code calls “Arcane”, alongside separate token, identity, and fraud detection services.

While we looked around, we could not find what SPAC stands for. If we’re allowed to guess, it could refer to “Samsung Private AI Cloud,” but it could just as easily be called something else. It’s early days, but it seems most of SPAC’s code deals with privacy and trust rather than AI. Based on the code, it appears to work in a few layers:

• A middleman for your requests: User requests appear to pass through a third-party relay first, so Samsung can see what you asked but not where it came from.

• Servers that have to prove themselves: Your phone appears to check that Samsung’s server is running genuine, untampered software before it sends anything.

• A public-style record: Samsung’s server software appears to be logged in a record that can’t be quietly changed, so it can’t swap in something different for some users.

• Anonymous passes: Your phone appears to get one-time passes that prove you’re a real Galaxy user without revealing which user you are.

The code also includes an “unattested” mode in which the phone skips some of these checks, but this could be for internal testing only.

Apple explained how Private Cloud Compute works back in June 2024, and Samsung’s SPAC looks remarkably similar so far.

SPAC’s code appears to have a match for almost every one of those pieces.

Apple isn’t the only one doing this. So far, it doesn’t seem like Samsung is inventing anything new here. It appears to be adopting what has become the industry’s standard recipe for private cloud AI, spelled out first by Apple. IntelliVoiceService references Gemma 4, while PhotoRemasterService references Black Forest Labs’ FLUX.2 klein 4B and a Stable Diffusion model.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Based on the code, several Galaxy AI features could use SPAC. AI select could get smarter at understanding what’s on your screen, for instance, pulling several events from a screenshot into your calendar at once. SPAC doesn’t seem to be live on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet

On our S26 Ultra, SPAC appears to be switched off for now:

• Smart Capture and Photo Editor only use SPAC on a newer Galaxy AI version than our S26 Ultra reports, the same gate as Recompose.

• PhotoRemasterService needs a newer Remaster version than the S26 Ultra has.

• IntelliVoiceService only uses SPAC for translation when an app asks for a “private” cloud mode, and we could not trigger this yet.

We used Writing assist, AI select, Note assist, Now Brief, and Interpreter while logging the phone’s activity. None of them touched SPAC, and all of them used Samsung’s existing Galaxy AI cloud or ran on the device. There’s also no user-facing text about SPAC anywhere in the build, so there’s no new consent screen or privacy notice yet. Samsung’s servers, on the other hand, appear to be further along than the phone software. Public certificate records show production server addresses for SPAC that Samsung has kept renewing over the past few months, and newer entries suggest it’s adding servers in the US as well.

The back end for SPAC could already be in place, waiting for the features to switch on.

A private cloud could matter for Galaxy AI

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

If SPAC works as the early code in this beta suggests, Samsung could swap today’s “not stored by Samsung” policy promise for one it can prove: running more powerful Galaxy AI features in the cloud while keeping your requests about as private as on-device processing.

Such a change would put Galaxy AI on equal footing with Apple Intelligence and Gemini on privacy. It could also matter more if Samsung starts charging for Galaxy AI Premium and leans harder on server-side models.

We’ve reached out to Samsung for more details on SPAC, and we’ll update this article when we hear back.

LG's S6FTR 5.1 soundbar with rear speakers is $180 off

LG's 5.1-channel soundbar kit with a subwoofer and wireless rear speakers is 45% off, its lowest price yet.

LG’s S6FTR soundbar kit just dropped to its lowest price. The complete 5.1-channel system is down to $219.99 on Amazon, which is $180 off its $399.99 list price and $30 below its previous low of $249.99.

The LG S6FTR comes with everything you need for surround sound in one box. Alongside the main soundbar, there’s a subwoofer for deeper bass and a pair of rear speakers to place behind your seating. With Dolby Audio support, effects in movies and games can move around the room instead of coming only from the front.

The rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, with no extra receiver needed. They are linked to each other with a cable, and one of them plugs into the wall, so it’s worth planning your layout around a nearby outlet.

Owners of compatible LG TVs get an extra perk. WOW Orchestra lets the TV’s speakers and the soundbar work together for a fuller sound, and it’s a neat way to get more out of hardware you already have.

The setup is a good fit for living rooms where a TV’s built-in speakers struggle with dialogue and bass, and it’s much simpler than piecing together a receiver and separate speakers.

At $219.99, the LG S6FTR is one of the more affordable ways to get true 5.1 surround sound with real rear speakers this holiday season.

Apple’s toughest smartwatch just hit a new low. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 (GPS + Cellular, 49mm) is down to $649.99 on Amazon, which is $149 off its $799 list price and the lowest price we’ve seen for it. Its best price before today was $699.99, and several band styles share the deal.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is designed for people who push their gear hard. A 49mm titanium case surrounds an always-on display that peaks at 3,000 nits, so it stays readable in bright sunlight on the trail or the water. items.title: Apple Still Working on Giant Foldable iPad That Could Cost $5,000
items.summary: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "…
items.body: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000. Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market. Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential. The comments follow a report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed. Gurman discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. The potential 2029 timeframe was already part of Gurman's report from October 2025 , when weight and display technology issues were said to threaten Apple's earlier 2028 target. • We also found a relocated speedometer in Google Maps, plus a bunch of new manufacturer icons that could land in a future update.

Android Auto is no stranger to bugs, and a future version of the app could make it easier to submit your device/car information in bug reports. Google is working on an updated Connected vehicles page with a new option to instantly copy and share relevant details.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We examined Android Auto version 18.3.164844 to enable a new Details option from the Android Auto settings page. This opens a “Vehicle information” dialog containing all the necessary information, including the car’s make and model, software version, display dimensions, and more.

As you would expect, the display details in the Vehicle information dialog are visible only when you’re connected to Android Auto. Meanwhile, there’s a Copy option here that lets you paste all these details into a bug report instantly.

When available, this new Details option should appear on the Connected vehicles page, accessible by tapping Vehicles in Android Auto settings, then tapping your car’s name. Currently, this page only contains the Forget and Rename options.

While we managed to uncover visuals of the new Details page in Android Auto settings, a string in the app’s code reveals another future addition.

Code

<string name="locked_app_not_supported_toast">This app is locked and cannot be opened in Android Auto</string>

Users will likely see the above toast when trying to open an Android Auto-compatible app that’s been locked via the upcoming app lock functionality. While app lock isn’t widely available on Android just yet, this string suggests Google is laying the groundwork for its future arrival.

Additionally, the Google Maps experience in Android Auto could get a minor tweak, with the speedometer icon moving from the bottom-left of the screen to the top-left. This opens up space in the bottom-left portion of the screen, which can sometimes be blocked by the speedometer.

Lastly, Android Auto is in the process of adding new OEM icons to the system. We’re seeing a handful of popular OEMs here, including some motorcycle brands.

The icon typically appears as the first option in the app drawer, as shown in the second screenshot above. Tapping this icon lets users exit the Android Auto experience instantly.

Since we had to manually activate some of these features, it’s hard to say when Android Auto will incorporate these changes. All we can do is hope that it happens sooner rather than later.

We examined Android Auto version 18.3.164844 to enable a new Details option from the Android Auto settings page. This opens a “Vehicle information” dialog containing all the necessary information, including the car’s make and model, software version, display dimensions, and more.

As you would expect, the display details in the Vehicle information dialog are visible only when you’re connected to Android Auto. Meanwhile, there’s a Copy option here that lets you paste all these details into a bug report instantly.

When available, this new Details option should appear on the Connected vehicles page, accessible by tapping Vehicles in Android Auto settings, then tapping your car’s name. Currently, this page only contains the Forget and Rename options.

Users will likely see the above toast when trying to open an Android Auto-compatible app that’s been locked via the upcoming app lock functionality. While app lock isn’t widely available on Android just yet, this string suggests Google is laying the groundwork for its future arrival.

Additionally, the Google Maps experience in Android Auto could get a minor tweak, with the speedometer icon moving from the bottom-left of the screen to the top-left. This opens up space in the bottom-left portion of the screen, which can sometimes be blocked by the speedometer.
Lastly, Android Auto is in the process of adding new OEM icons to the system. We’re seeing a handful of popular OEMs here, including some motorcycle brands.
The icon typically appears as the first option in the app drawer, as shown in the second screenshot above. Tapping this icon lets users exit the Android Auto experience instantly.
Since we had to manually activate some of these features, it’s hard to say when Android Auto will incorporate these changes. All we can do is hope that it happens sooner rather than later.

iPhones Dominate China's Weak Singles' Day Smartphone Sales

Thursday November 26, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple held the top spot in China's smartphone market during the country's Singles' Day shopping festival, despite an 8% year-over-year sales decline, according to Counterpoint Research. The overall market fell 17% across the promotional period, defined as weeks 42–46.

Six of the top 10 bestsellers were iPhone 17 and 18 models, led by the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the iPhone Duo at No. 9. Huawei was the only major brand to grow in the period, rising by 29%. Counterpoint says buyers are postponing upgrades rather than accepting higher prices, following strong iPhone 18 Pro sales in China at launch.

items.summary: Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.

Mobile

You can now change YouTube’s app icon on your phone, but only if you pay for it

Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:32 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• YouTube is now letting Premium subscribers change its app icon.

• The current selection includes three options for the icon.

• YouTube has been testing seven app icons in total, but four are missing from the current rollout.

Several prominent apps, including X, Telegram, Reddit, and Instagram, let users swap out the default app icon for something else. Often, this perk is available only to users who pay for the experience. Last month, we learned that YouTube is also working on a similar feature that lets Premium subscribers change the app icon, and it already appears to be rolling out for some folks.

User Radu Oncescu on X posted screenshots of the setting that lets users change the default icon to one of the three other options currently available. These include one with a shiny, metal-like finish, somewhat like a silver YouTube Play button, another one featuring what look like brush strokes using red paint, and a third one with a pixel effect and a gradient over the icon.

X / Radu Oncescu

These options appear under Settings > General > Premium app icon inside the YouTube app. While we spotted the feature being tested on Android, the user notes that it’s available on iOS. Another report from user howfxr on X last week suggests the feature also cropped up for some Android users.

X / howfxr

In both cases, the rollout does not seem to be widespread, and we don’t have it on any of our devices yet. So we recommend not fretting if you don’t have it either yet. It’s not like YouTube is bringing back the original logo with the name spelled out anyway.

Meanwhile, YouTube has been testing four more icon options, including some retro ones, but none appear to be available for now. We’ll keep an eye out for when those might be available.
